Issued at 200 PM EDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Currently-Tonight... KMLB radar imagery showers east moving 
scattered showers and lightning storms over east central Florida 
to the south of the Orlando Metro. GOES-16 satellite imagery and
local observations indicate partly to mostly cloudy skies.
Temperatures are currently in the upper 80s to low 90s with dew
points in the mid 70s to around 80 degrees, in addition to heat
index values up to 100-109F degrees. Analysis charts show a
mid/upper level trough over the southwest Atlantic and northern
Florida with areas of PVA embedded within the base of the trough.
Additionally, the Atlantic ridge is positioned well to the east-southeast
of east central Florida. 

A Heat Advisory remains in effect until 7PM for Lake, Volusia, 
Orange, Seminole, and northern Brevard county this evening. 
Isolated to scattered generally east moving showers (20-60% 
chance) and lightning storms are forecast to increase in coverage 
into the late afternoon and evening hours. The greatest chance for
showers and lightning storms are along the Orlando Metro and to 
the south. WSW winds at 5-10mph are forecast to back onshore with 
the east coast sea breeze mainly north of the Treasure Coast to 
the east of the Orlando Metro into this evening. WSW winds at 
5-10mph are forecast to back onshore with the east coast sea 
breeze mainly north of the Treasure Coast to the east of the 
Orlando Metro into this evening. The potential exists for isolated
strong storms today capable of producing wind gusts up to 
40-50mph, frequent lightning, and heavy rainfall (1-3"+ in 
30-60mins). Rain chances are expected to diminish towards sunset.
Above normal (1-4+ degrees) lows in the mid to upper 70s are 
forecast.

Wednesday-Thursday... Drier air is expected tomorrow with an 
increase in WSW flow and no east coast sea breeze. WSW winds are 
expected to increase into the afternoon at 10-15mph with gusts to 
20-25mph. Isolated to scattered showers and lightning storms are 
forecast to develop in the afternoon and evening with the greatest
chance for showers and storms again along and to the south of the
Orlando Metro. The potential exists for isolated strong storms
capable of producing wind gusts up to 40-50mph, frequent
lightning, and heavy rainfall (1-3"+ in 30-60mins). Afternoon
highs in the low to mid 90s are forecast on Wednesday. A Heat 
Advisory is in effect from 11AM to 8PM for heat index up to 110F 
degrees for Lake, Volusia, Orange, Seminole, and northern Brevard 
county Wednesday. Moisture will increase on Thursday with PWATs up
to 2.0-2.5" as a stationary boundary sags south across the 
southern US. Remember to practice heat safety which includes
shifting work away from the hours of 10AM-4PM, wear light
clothing, drink plenty of fluids, and take frequent breaks from
the heat. 

Guidance is not in good agreement on the timing of 
showers and storms on Thursday. The CAMs aren't showing much 
except for the HRRR, however, the global models are in decent 
agreement on a line of showers and storms tracking southeast 
across east central Florida early Thursday morning. however, it 
appears there will be two potential time periods for strong to 
severe storms to develop on Thursday. The first will be early 
Thursday morning after 12AM and generally before 8AM with 
additional development into the afternoon and evening hours. 
Instability is expected to be high with MLCAPE up to 1,500-3,800 
J/kg, 0-6km shear up to 15-40kts, and a LLJ up to 25-30kts, 
especially Thursday afternoon and evening. The SPC has outlooked
northern Lake and Volusia counties with a Marginal Risk (level 1
of 5) for severe storms early Thursday morning. The main hazards
are wind gusts up to 60mph, frequent lightning, and heavy rainfall
(1-3" in 30-60mins with a 1 in 10 chance of totals in excess of 3"
up to 3-6"). A Marginal Risk (5-14% risk) for Excessive Rainfall 
exists for much of east central Floria on Thursday with the 
potential for flooding of roadways and low-lying areas. Slightly
cooler temperatures are expected with the increase in rain chances
and cloud cover. Afternoon highs in the upper 80s to low 90s and
above normal lows (1-4F+ degrees) in the mid to upper 70s are
forecast.

Friday-Monday... A relatively active weather pattern is expected 
with a stationary boundary over the southern US with the NBM
probability of precipitation (PoPs) remaining high through the 
weekend. However, the trend for the most part has been for the NBM
to have too high of PoPs in the extended forecast and MOS data
suggests that is likely the case this weekend with offshore flow
and no sea breeze. Scattered to numerous showers (60%-90% 
chance) and lightning storms are forecast on Friday with rain
